text:
maya: Heads-up: spotted weird delta in the mini-burn widget for dev-sandbox — per-invocation cost shows negative "cache savings" on some routes.
alex: Hmm. Seen briefly. Looks like when sticky routing + shared prefetch slab = zero-prefetch charge but we still attribute prefetched tokens to origin route? Could flip sign.
chen: Can you paste the query id / sample payload? I want to repro. Also which model sku? (gpt-j-6b-quant?)
maya: sample id `req_20240301_7b` — model=gpt-j-6b-ql8, route=/chat/stream, tenant=dev-sandbox
lina: i'm seeing similar in the heatmap. The console's per-route panel aggregates "prefetch credits" differently than the costlineage API. UX mismatch.
dave: suspect telemetry mismatch: batcher emits prefetch_used but meter pipeline applies a negative cache credit when origin attribution is null. Quick hack in proto: `if origin == null -> credit = 0` might avoid negative entries.
alex: if we do that, we'll change invoices for test tenants; better to correct attribution earlier (router should synthesize origin route id for shared prefetches).
chen: repro script (local):
```
POST /v1/generate
{ "model": "gpt-j-6b-ql8", "input": "...", "route_hint": "dev-sandbox:shared-prefetch" }
```
then check /api/costlineage?req=req_20240301_7b

maya: ops-bot noted a canary deploy around then:
ops-bot: deploy: canary/graphite-routes v2.3.1 -> prod (started by ci/cd)

lina: ok, plan: (1) fix router to synthesize origin for shared-prefetch (2) add unit test for null-origin crediting (3) patch console to ignore negative credits in UI as a stopgap. Thoughts?
dave: +1. Also add an alert for negative total-savings in the per-tenant burn job (pager if > 0.1% of last 24h).
alex: threading into backlog: ENG-plat #4821 (router origin synth), #4822 (meter guard) — i'll pick #4822
maya: thanks. i'll add a quick example in the analytics docs so SREs don't misinterpret negative spikes :thumbsup:
